doc.title: David Torkanowsky interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, September 26, 2019

title: The one time he fired a drummer
summary: George Porter's trio with Troy Davis, whose sub Simon Lot played so well he was kept.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: I’m going to turn to a question around that I asked earlier about why of five piano players does one get the gig. What would cause you, if you had a steady gig somewhere and you had sidemen and sidewomen, what would cause you to fire somebody?

I only did that one time. I had a trio gig in New Orleans, George Porter was the bass player, great drummer named Troy Davis, who played a lot with who’s the Jamaican piano player, Monty Alexander, a really good player, played with Terence Blanchard one

time or two, a really great New Orleans drummer. He was going out for a month with Monty. And I said well just send me somebody good. And he sent one of his students, a brilliant drummer named Simon Lot. So he called me a month later and he goes, “Hey bro I’m back in town, what’s up?” And I go, “Bro, I don’t really know how to tell you this but the guy you sent played you off the gig.” He was that good. This cat had perfect balance. He sounded — he made everything we played sound like a Blue Note record. He was killer. Had good drumming bass chops, you know, he had all the language. And so I’ve never done that before or since and he’s probably still a little pissed at me for it, but what would cause me to fire somebody? Bad attitude or ineptitude. ‘tude.
‘Tude. Yeah. Some you need, some you don’t.
